# Independent legacy base-format evidence

The controlled `baseline.ods` / `changed.ods` and `baseline.xls` / `changed.xls` pairs were authored through LibreOffice UNO, then independently closed and reopened on 2026-10-23. Producer/readback: LibreOfficeDev 26.8.0.0.alpha0, build `2c87e51eeaa2b413ff4ae097b2705eea1995d8e5`. `ReadStyles.java` is the complete producer/reader; it never imports application code. The XLS filter is `MS Excel 97`; the ODS filter is `calc8`.

All document loads explicitly use named `MacroExecMode.NEVER_EXECUTE` and `UpdateDocMode.NO_UPDATE`, with Hidden and ReadOnly. The fresh local UNO profile/listener is isolated and terminates after readback. No external resources are requested. `libreoffice-readback.txt` is the raw independent result; `independent-readback.json` mechanically transcribes its tab-separated fields, without any application-derived expected styles.

Both workbooks have identical numeric values, 123.25, in A1:A6 and A8:A9. A7 is an explicitly formatted blank. Differences isolate font size/weight/color (A1), fill (A2), bottom border (A3), horizontal alignment/wrap/rotation (A4), protection flags (A5), number format (A6), and blank-cell fill (A7). Column B and row 10 have changing default fills. B10 is an explicit blank with the same fill in both files, overriding both defaults. A8/A9 remain ordinary defaults. Readback also samples B1, A10 and C10 to qualify sparse default semantics.

The XLS exporter substitutes authored Liberation Sans with stored Arial; both the native census and independent XLS reload report Arial. The exporter retains a US locale prefix in stored custom number-format codes, while UNO FormatString readback omits that prefix. Independent tests strip only the known `[$-409]` prefix for these authored XLS formats; source comparison must still retain exact format codes. ODS and XLS readback are retained separately rather than incorrectly asserting every producer detail survives conversion.

## Genuine XLSB evidence and limits

No XLSB fixture was generated by this project. The same restricted UNO reader sampled the first 12 rows / 6 columns of every sheet of existing pinned, independently sourced files:

- [`pandas-test1.xlsb`](../../xlsb-fixtures/README.md): official pandas fixture, existing pinned commit/hash and BSD license. Readback qualifies Calibri 11/12 point font, bold headers, black colors, thin bottom borders, centered alignment and stored default protection. Date formats are observed but their exact spelling is localized by LibreOffice.
- [`issues.xlsb` and `issue_182.xlsb`](../../xlsb-formula-fixtures/README.md): existing pinned Calamine fixtures and MIT license. Readback qualifies additional U2400/U0400 fonts, 14 point text and white font color, plus General/integer formats. VBA payloads are never executed.

Tests compare actual sampled formatting to the census, including the sparse defaults at sampled blank coordinates. Exact number-format assertions for XLSB are limited to General and integer `0`; the readback's localized date spelling does not prove exact original format-code identity. Font fallback/theme script metadata, all border sides, theme tint fidelity, rich text, nondefault XLSB fills/protection/rotation and full worksheets are **not** independently qualified by these samples. Separate synthetic binary mutations can test implementation mechanics but must not be labelled independent producer evidence.

Reproduction requires a JDK, the official LibreOffice Java UNO library (used `org.libreoffice:libreoffice:24.2.7`), and the bundled `soffice`. Compile `ReadStyles.java`, start a fresh isolated `--headless --norestore --nodefault --nofirststartwizard` profile with a local UNO listener on port 20424, then invoke the class with the absolute output folder followed by the three XLSB input paths. The class loads using the named restrictions above and terminates its desktop. Archive timestamps can differ. `sha256.json` pins retained generated artifacts and existing XLSB inputs.

## Labelled derived XLSB semantic qualification

`derived-formatting.xlsb` is **not** an independently produced XLSB. `derive-xlsb.cjs` changes only `xl/styles.bin` in pinned pandas-test1.xlsb and verifies every other part payload remains byte-identical. It changes the first fill record to solid RGB `123456`, the first border's top edge to thin red, and every cell-XF to left alignment, wrapping, rotation byte 100, indent 2, unlocked/hidden protection. Parent style-XF records are deliberately retained unchanged. Original font records and values remain untouched.

The restricted independent UNO reader reopens these changed bytes and records its interpretation in `derived-libreoffice-readback.txt` / `derived-readback.json`. LibreOffice reports rotation 350 degrees, equivalent to the intended -10 degrees; the comparison uses this explicit modulo-360 normalization. The sampled properties qualify nondefault fill, alignment/wrap/rotation and protection semantics for this labelled derived input. The top-border mutation is not independently qualified by the current reader, which records only bottom edges.

This control also exposed a distinction between cell-XF zero and the implicit default: explicit cells/column defaults take the modified cell-XF alignment/protection, but implicit blank cells retain the original parent/default-style alignment and protection. A census cannot automatically apply modified cell-XF zero to every absent cell. The independent test preserves this distinction rather than dropping the blank-cell assertions.
